sde_bench_run.evaluation_scope: public sample transaction output; internal synthetic-only split, first partition as reference and second partition as evaluated synthetic set
sde_bench_run.export_command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m sde_bench amlsim-export --input data/public_raw/amlsim/tx.csv --out-dir reports/public_benchmarks/amlsim --format jsonl
sde_bench_run.evaluate_command: PYTHONPATH=src python -m sde_bench evaluate --real reports/public_benchmarks/amlsim/reference.jsonl --synthetic reports/public_benchmarks/amlsim/synthetic.jsonl --source reports/public_benchmarks/amlsim/source.jsonl --target transaction_type --preset core_eval --json-out reports/public_benchmarks/amlsim/report.json --md-out reports/public_benchmarks/amlsim/report.md

interpretation_notes: This is a small public AMLSim sample, not a full-scale AML benchmark run.
The common SDE-Bench core axes are reused for finance, so fidelity/diversity/privacy are meaningful but medical-only axes are intentionally omitted.
Utility is transaction-type population coverage because the sample has no downstream fraud labels or analyst predictions.
